items.title: Alton Purnell Interview, 1958-08-29
items.q: when Earl Hines was popular, he would, when he'd sit down at the piano he liked the kid, he would listen on it

ctx.x: Who was the, I guess you sort of picked your pianist saying Vernell, San Diego was the best and greatest you ever heard. Would you say that or who would be your favorite? Well. Of the New Orleans pianos.

I wouldn't have to say Vernell was my favorite piano player, although he couldn't read. But there was nothing that he heard that he couldn't play. I mean when Earl Hines was popular, he would, when he'd sit down at the piano he liked the kid, he would listen on it and he was a lot of fun. And he would listen at a record and he'd play like that record. Then he would play, then he'd say this is the way I would play it.
